# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [blue] [yellow] [blue]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[2] 2:[9] 3:[0] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[red] 4:[purple] 5:[orange] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👌 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👆 👐 🙏]

**Thinking:**
I am Deaf. I see the bomb's physical state but cannot hear or touch it. The other monkeys (Mute and Blind) are trying to communicate with me via gestures, which is my only input channel besides what I see on the display/wires.

My current view:
- Display: 6
- Light: Red
- Strip: Blue, Yellow, Blue
- Keypad: Engraved numbers 1:[2], 2:[9], 3:[0], 4:[8]. It says "[1 digits]" and "[entered nothing]". This likely means I need to enter a single digit code into the keypad.
- Wires: 1:Blue, 2:White, 3:Red, 4:Purple, 5:Orange, 6:Green.

The Mute has read the manual. The Blind can touch the bomb. They are gesturing at me.
Mute gesture 1: 👆 (Up/One), 👌 (OK/Zero?), ✌ (Two).
Mute gesture 2: 👌 (OK/Zero?), ✌ (Two).
Blind gesture: 👆 (Up/One), 👐 (Open hands?), 🙏 (Prayer/Thanks?).

These gestures are ambiguous without a shared language. However, the Mute *reads the manual*. If the manual specifies how to interpret these gestures, the Mute might be trying to tell me the rule or the answer directly. But since I don't know the gesture-to-meaning mapping yet, I should probably try to establish communication or ask for clarification through the channels available to them. Wait, I cannot speak to Mute effectively if they are Mute? No, "Mute" means they cannot speak, but they can read/gesture. I can speak to Mute (they receive speech textually? No, "Speech is a voice... whoever can hear receives your words"). Mute cannot hear? The table says Mute "Cannot Speak, or touch the bomb". It doesn't explicitly say Mute cannot hear. Usually "Mute" implies inability to speak, not hear. "Deaf" implies inability to hear. So Mute CAN hear me. Blind CANNOT see gestures, but CAN hear me.

So:
- I (Deaf) cannot hear anyone. I can see gestures from Mute and Blind.
- Mute can hear me (speech) and see gestures. Cannot speak.
- Blind can hear me (speech) and feel the bomb. Cannot see gestures or colors.

Strategy:
1. I need to convey what I see to Blind so he can act on the wires/display.
2. I need to understand what Mute wants me to do or knows from the manual.
3. Since Mute is gesturing at me, they are trying to send information. I should acknowledge receipt or ask for clarification by speaking to Mute (who can hear me) and Blind (who can hear me).

Let's look at the Keypad again. `1:[2] 2:[9] 3:[0] 4:[8]`. This looks like button labels. Button 1 shows '2', Button 2 shows '9', etc. Or maybe it's a sequence? `[1 digits]` suggests the code length is 1. `[entered nothing]` means no input yet.

If I speak, both Mute and Blind will hear my words.
I will describe the visual state clearly to Blind, as he needs to manipulate the bomb based on visual cues he can't see.
I will also ask Mute to clarify their gestures, perhaps by pointing to specific parts of the bomb if possible, or just stating that I am confused by the hand signs.

Actually, looking at the gestures again:
Mute: 👆 👌 ✌ -> Maybe "1, 0, 2"? Or "Point up, OK, Peace".
Mute: 👌 ✌ -> "0, 2"?
Blind: 👆 👐 🙏 -> "1, Open Hands, Pray".

This seems like a puzzle where the gestures correspond to actions or codes. Without knowing the dictionary, I'm stuck. However, usually in these puzzles, standard emojis have meanings.
👆 = Up / 1
👌 = OK / Zero / Circle
✌ = Two / V
👐 = Open / Spread
🙏 = Please / Thanks / High Five?

If Mute is reading the manual, maybe the manual defines these gestures.
I will speak to everyone, describing the bomb's current state precisely so Blind can act, and asking Mute to confirm if the gestures relate to the keypad or wires.

Key info for Blind:
- Display shows 6.
- Light is Red.
- Strip is Blue-Yellow-Blue.
- Keypad has 4 buttons labeled 1, 2, 3, 4. Their engraved faces show 2, 9, 0, 8 respectively.
- Wire colors: 1-Blue, 2-White, 3-Red, 4-Purple, 5-Orange, 6-Green.

I'll start by broadcasting this visual data. Then I'll address the gestures.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Display shows 6. Light is red. Strip is blue yellow blue. Keypad has four buttons. Button 1 face shows 2. Button 2 face shows 9. Button 3 face shows 0. Button 4 face shows 8. Status says 1 digit needed, nothing entered. Wires: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see your gestures: finger up, ok sign, peace sign; then ok sign, peace sign. Blind gestured: finger up, open hands, praying hands. Do these refer to the keypad numbers or wire positions? I cannot hear you, please use gestures to indicate if I should press a button or cut a wire, or speak to Blind to guide him.")
wait()
```
